clue.text: Losing toss one turns into scholars

indicators.note: turns into says the preceding letters change shape and become something new

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A gambler who keeps losing the coin toss becomes studious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' rearranges LOSING, TOSS and I (from 'one') into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinologists are academics who study Chinese language, history and culture, so they are scholars.

clue.text: God climbs into it, being awkward

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbs means the word goes upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity clambering into something looks clumsy doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbs' reads the god upwards; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or lacking skill, close to clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Bit of Greek in a moronic translation

indicators.note: a translation renders words into a new form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek text has been rendered by a dim-witted translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges MORONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a small piece of Greek.

clue.text: Pieces of gold in circulation?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
bits are pieces

explanation.surface: Gold coins are passing from hand to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests money in circulation; the answer is going round as a planet does, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that orbits travels round and round a body, a playful kind of circulation.

clue.text: False dreams make one sick with us and possibly in love

parts.note: sick means ill
taken as written

indicators.note: possibly says the word may be arranged in a different order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Imagining being in love can leave a person and their partner feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IN plus O (love) into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: False dreams are deceptive fancies, which together create a mistaken belief or delusion.

clue.text: Start taking success to a girl in that place

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: a hit is a success
her refers to any girl or woman

explanation.surface: Someone sets off in a bid to take a triumph back to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Thither is an old word meaning to that spot or over there.

clue.text: For clergymen one is cast differently under a place in Lancashire

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means this part sits beneath the place name

parts.note: Eccles is a town near Manchester, historically in Lancashire
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: differently says the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Clergy are being assigned new roles in a parish in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges IS CAST into ASTICS. ECCLES is a town near Manchester, famous for Eccles cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastics are churchmen, members of the clergy.

clue.text: The complaint about Hardy is mine

indicators.note: about says one word goes round the other

parts.note: a cry is a complaint or protest
Oliver (Ollie) Hardy was the comedian of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A grievance about Thomas Hardy's writing is claimed as one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests Thomas the novelist; it is Ollie of Laurel and Hardy. 'mine' is a noun, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine with its buildings.

clue.text: Showing spirit on the street with a sailor

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit
St is the abbreviation for street
a rating is a sailor without officer rank

explanation.surface: A ghost is protesting in the road alongside a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' looks like a noun but is a verb form, as in showing someone how.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstrating means displaying or exhibiting, as one does when explaining by example.

clue.text: Cover me with an animal

parts.note: a coat is a covering
me becomes I, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be wrapped up along with a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted mammal of the raccoon family from the Americas.

clue.text: American city is evil about eastern island

indicators.note: about says one word goes round another

parts.note: bale is an archaic word for evil or woe
Timor is an island in South-East Asia

explanation.surface: A city in the USA is said to be wicked to a far-off island.
explanation.walkthrough: BALE as evil survives in baleful.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a large port city in Maryland.

clue.text: The learned man could get a result without it

indicators.note: could get suggests the letters can be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A scholar claims he could reach the answer without the tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' rearranges A RESULT plus IT; 'without' (outside) is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A literatus is a man of letters, a learned scholar.

clue.text: An awful place with nothing welcome

parts.note: hell is a dreadful place
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dreadful spot with nobody in it gives a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is a greeting, the word used to welcome someone.

clue.text: A container in a direction belonging to an ancient place

indicators.note: in says these pieces are placed inside another

parts.note: SE is south-east, a compass direction
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: A receptacle found pointing one way at an old archaeological site.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabine relates to the Sabines, an old Italic people of the region near Rome.

clue.text: Bachelors hold almost the opposite of objection to washing facilities

indicators.note: hold says the first word keeps others inside it

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, so bachelors are BAs

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its final letter
opposite of turns the following word round, reading it backwards

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Single men put up a fight against sharing the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite of' turns the objection round into a word for a bath; 'Bachelors' are BAs, plural, so the S closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathtubs are large containers people wash in.

clue.text: Grimness which would do for our headland if it lost its head

parts.words: which would do for our headland if it lost its head
parts.note: remove the first letter and what is left splits as a phrase meaning our promontory, NESS being a headland

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood would suit our cape if it were beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or place names like Foulness on the British coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dourness is a stern, sullen severity, much the same as grimness.

clue.text: Medical man holds what goes through Preston is a footballer

indicators.note: holds says one word contains another

parts.note: Dr is a doctor
the River Ribble flows through Preston in Lancashire

explanation.surface: A doctor's grip on a Preston matter turns out to be about a player.
explanation.walkthrough: Preston is a town in Lancashire, north-west England, on the River Ribble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dribbler is a player who runs with the ball at the feet, a footballer.

clue.text: Skill which produces a score after one is held by a potential star

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the rest
is held by says this piece goes inside another
potential suggests something that could be formed, so the word is arranged again

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a try is a score in rugby

explanation.surface: Talent produces points once a budding celebrity steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges STAR into ARTS. In rugby a try scores points, which is why 'a score' gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship.

clue.text: Is metal in the London area named after a pope?

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside another

parts.note: SE is a London postal district (south-east)
taken as written
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is metal in a part of London named for a pontiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sistine Chapel takes its name from Pope Sixtus IV.

clue.text: You are held by a cham-. pion, one who shows powers of endurance

definitions.text: one who shows powers of endurance

indicators.note: are held by says this piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a champion is a star
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: You are in the grip of a champion, a person with great stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'cham-. pion' is a line break in 'champion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or athlete with stamina, able to last a long race.

clue.text: Food depicted in the front page inside a cover put back

indicators.note: inside says the piece is placed within another
put back turns the words round so they read backwards

parts.note: a coat is a cover
the front page is page one, P plus I

explanation.surface: A dish is pictured on the newspaper's front page, inside a jacket that was replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses A COAT to TAOCA. The front page of a paper is page one, P plus the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy food from cassava, often made into puddings.

clue.text: Start teaching a beginner in a loud song without qualifications

parts.note: f is forte, loud in music

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside another word

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: start picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on cars

explanation.surface: Someone begins teaching a novice to sing loudly despite having no credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies an unqualified teacher; the definition means bluntly, without reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something flatly is to say it plainly, with no hedging or reservations.

clue.text: Latin gives the bird to America

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A Roman hands a small bird over to the Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives the bird' suggests booing or a rude gesture; it simply supplies TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is a Latin name, borne by a Roman emperor.

clue.text: There is a fielder pursuing the delivery, it writes

indicators.note: pursuing puts this piece after the other one

parts.note: a ball is a delivery from a bowler in cricket
point is a cricket fielding position on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder chases the ball after it is bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler's delivery is a ball, and point is a fielding position square of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, an instrument for writing.

clue.text: Fire which decapitates one

indicators.note: decapitates means the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A blaze is something that beheads a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fireplace or the fire burning in a hearth, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Of a different calibre to an old vehicle

indicators.note: different says the letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something of another quality compared with an antique car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges CALIBRE plus TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet was a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a vintage conveyance.

clue.text: Instrument used by major — gang

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big criminal gang employs a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a keyboard musical instrument with pipes.

clue.text: A player gets excited, revealing the way to Heaven

indicators.note: excited suggests agitated motion, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A sportsman gets worked up, showing the route to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges A PLAYER GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly gates are the traditional entrance to Heaven.
